R.name: Realistic
R.summary: Realistic people think with their hands. You like seeing a result you can touch: a circuit that works, a building that stands, a garden that grows, a car that starts on the first try. You would rather fix the bike than write an essay about it. At school you probably enjoyed practicals more than theory, and you are often the one relatives call when the Wi-Fi, the TV or the car stops working. You value skill, competence and getting things done, and you are happiest with clear problems, tools, machines, outdoor work or physical activity.

careers.title: Civil Engineer
careers.route: Accredited civil engineering degree (BEng, BSc or BE), then supervised work experience towards a professional licence (PE, CEng or P.Eng), which differs by country.
careers.outlook: Steady worldwide: housing, transport, water and climate-resilient infrastructure all need engineers, and Gulf megaprojects keep hiring. AI speeds up design, not site judgement.

careers.title: Mechanical Engineer
careers.route: Accredited mechanical engineering degree; degree apprenticeships (UK) and co-op programmes (Canada, US) let you earn while you study. Chartered or licensed status comes after experience.
careers.outlook: Steady in manufacturing, energy, HVAC and automotive; electric vehicles, clean energy and Gulf project roles are the growth areas.

careers.title: Electrical / Power Engineer
careers.route: Electrical or electronic engineering degree (power or electronics track) plus internships or co-ops; professional licensing follows a few years of supervised work, with rules set by each country.
careers.outlook: Growing fast as countries add solar, wind, grid upgrades, battery storage and data centres, which all need power engineers.

careers.title: Mechatronics & Robotics Engineer
careers.route: Degree in mechatronics, robotics, mechanical or electrical engineering; robotics clubs, competitions and a portfolio of builds count heavily for internships and first jobs.
careers.outlook: Emerging and well paid as automation spreads through factories, warehouses, hospitals and farms, helped by AI-driven robots.

careers.title: Solar PV Technician / Installer
careers.route: No degree needed: a short solar installation course (weeks to months), on-the-job training and whatever electrical or safety certification your country requires.
careers.outlook: Booming: rooftop and commercial solar is one of the world's fastest-growing trades in 2026, from Texas to the Gulf to South Asia.

careers.title: Electrician / HVAC Technician
careers.route: Paid apprenticeship or vocational college course after school, then a trade licence; the number of training years and licensing rules differ by country and state.
careers.outlook: Constant demand everywhere; heat pumps, EV chargers and Gulf construction keep skilled trades short of people, and AI can't rewire a house.

careers.title: Auto & EV Technician
careers.route: Automotive apprenticeship at a dealership or garage, or a vocational diploma after school; manufacturer and high-voltage EV certifications raise your pay quickly.
careers.outlook: Steady; hybrid and EV repair skills are a fast-growing, well-paid niche as electric cars spread.

careers.title: Armed Forces Officer
careers.route: Officer academy straight after school, or officer training after a degree; selection includes aptitude tests, fitness, medicals and interviews. Most forces require citizenship.
careers.outlook: Stable, respected careers with regular annual intakes; technical, cyber and engineering branches are growing.

careers.title: Agriculture Scientist / Agritech Specialist
careers.route: Degree in agriculture, plant or soil science, or environmental science; data, drone and GIS skills help, and research roles usually need a master's.
careers.outlook: Growing interest in agritech, vertical farming, water efficiency and climate-smart food production worldwide.

careers.title: CAD Drafter / 3D Modeller (remote)
careers.route: No university degree needed: short courses and certifications in AutoCAD, Revit or SolidWorks, plus a strong portfolio for firms and freelance platforms.
careers.outlook: Remote drafting and BIM work for international firms is a growing niche; AI tools reward people who understand how buildings actually go together.

careers.title: Chef / Culinary Professional
careers.route: Culinary school diploma or a kitchen apprenticeship straight after school; many top chefs learn entirely on the job, working up from prep cook.
careers.outlook: Restaurants, cloud kitchens, hotels and Gulf hospitality keep demand steady, and desi food keeps winning new fans worldwide.

careers.title: Mobile & Electronics Repair Technician
careers.route: No degree needed: a short repair course or online training, then an apprenticeship at a repair shop; manufacturer certification helps you stand out.
careers.outlook: Every city needs one; right-to-repair laws and pricier phones mean skilled technicians often grow into their own shop.

R.subjects: Maths and Physics (plus Chemistry or Further Maths) at A-level, IB or advanced high-school level for engineering; Biology, Chemistry or Geography for agriculture; Design & Technology or a vocational or technical course for trades and apprenticeships.

I.name: Investigative
I.summary: Investigative people need to know why. You enjoy puzzles, patterns and questions without easy answers, and you would rather understand a problem fully than rush a quick fix. You may be the student who argues with the textbook, the cousin who fact-checks every forward in the family WhatsApp group, or the one who reads the leaflet before taking any medicine. You value logic, evidence and independence, and you are happiest when you can analyse, research, experiment and think deeply without constant interruption.
strengths: Curiosity and a love of learning

careers.title: Doctor
careers.route: Medical degree straight after school (MBBS or MBChB) or after a first degree (MD in the US and Canada), then residency and licensing exams that differ by country.
careers.outlook: Always needed; competition for seats and specialist training is intense everywhere, and AI is taking on paperwork and imaging support, not patient care.

careers.title: Pharmacist
careers.route: Pharmacy degree (MPharm, PharmD or BPharm, four to six years), then supervised practice and a registration exam; qualifications don't always transfer between countries.
careers.outlook: Steady in hospitals, community pharmacies, industry and regulatory affairs; pharmacists are taking on more clinical and prescribing roles.

careers.title: Software Engineer
careers.route: Computer science or software engineering degree, or a bootcamp plus self-taught projects; a GitHub portfolio and internships matter as much as the certificate.
careers.outlook: Strong local and remote demand, but AI coding tools have reshaped entry-level work, so real projects and problem-solving set you apart.

careers.title: Data Scientist / AI Engineer
careers.route: Degree in computer science, data science, statistics or maths, often with a master's; online specialisations and a portfolio of real projects on GitHub or Kaggle.
careers.outlook: One of the fastest-growing fields of 2026; employers want proof you can build, evaluate and deploy AI, not just certificates.

careers.title: Data Analyst (remote)
careers.route: Any degree helps but isn't essential: certificates in Excel, SQL, Power BI or Python, plus a portfolio of dashboards, can land your first role.
careers.outlook: High remote demand and a practical entry point into tech without an expensive degree; AI makes good analysts faster, not obsolete.

careers.title: Cybersecurity Analyst
careers.route: Cybersecurity or computing degree, or self-study certifications such as CompTIA Security+ with hands-on labs; many people start in IT support and move up.
careers.outlook: Growing everywhere as banks, hospitals and governments digitise and AI-powered attacks rise; strong remote options.

careers.title: Medical Lab Technologist / Biomedical Scientist
careers.route: Biomedical or medical laboratory science degree, or a shorter technician diploma in some countries, then registration with your country's health regulator.
careers.outlook: Steady demand in hospitals, private labs and diagnostic chains, with automation shifting work towards quality control.

careers.title: Clinical Psychologist
careers.route: Psychology degree, then a master's or doctorate in clinical psychology with supervised practice; titles and requirements are regulated differently in each country.
careers.outlook: Rising mental-health awareness, including in desi families, keeps demand growing in clinics, schools and online therapy.

careers.title: Economist / Policy Researcher
careers.route: Economics degree, usually followed by a master's for research roles; government economist schemes and think-tank internships are common ways in.
careers.outlook: Needed in central banks, think tanks, consultancies and development organisations; data and AI skills are now expected.

careers.title: Biotechnologist / Research Scientist
careers.route: Degree in biotechnology, biochemistry or molecular biology, then a funded master's or PhD; international scholarships make moving countries for research common.
careers.outlook: Growing with gene therapy, vaccines and AI-driven drug discovery; research careers often involve working in more than one country.

careers.title: Environmental / Climate Scientist
careers.route: Degree in environmental science, geography or earth sciences, with GIS and data skills; a master's helps for research and policy roles.
careers.outlook: Growing fast: climate adaptation, sustainability reporting, NGOs and international projects all need people who can read the data.

careers.title: Forensic Scientist
careers.route: Degree in forensic science, chemistry or biology; jobs are with police, government labs or private firms, and often need security clearance.
careers.outlook: A small, specialised field linked to policing and the courts; digital forensics is the fastest-growing branch.

I.subjects: Biology and Chemistry (with Physics or Maths) at A-level, IB or advanced high-school level for medicine, pharmacy and the life sciences; Maths and Computer Science for computing and data; Economics, Psychology and Statistics for the social sciences.

A.name: Artistic
A.summary: Artistic people see the world as raw material for something new. You notice colour, sound, words and design, and you would rather invent your own way than follow a template. You might be the one who designs the shaadi card, edits the family holiday video, writes poetry in your notes app, or rearranges the living-room furniture just to see how it looks. You value originality, self-expression and freedom, and you are happiest when your work lets you imagine, design, write, perform or create something people can feel.
strengths: An eye for beauty, design and detail
The ability to move and connect with people

careers.title: Architecture & Building Design
careers.route: Accredited architecture degree (five to seven years including practice), then a licensing exam; admission usually asks for a portfolio. Titles and routes differ by country.
careers.outlook: Steady in housing and urban projects; 3D visualisation, sustainable design and AI-assisted drafting add remote options.

careers.title: Graphic Designer (freelance)
careers.route: Design degree (BFA or BDes), or short courses and self-teaching; a strong portfolio on Behance or Instagram matters more than the certificate.
careers.outlook: A huge freelance category worldwide; AI image tools raise the bar, so clients pay for ideas, taste and brand thinking.

careers.title: UI/UX Designer
careers.route: Design, psychology or computing degree, or a UX bootcamp and Figma certificates; a portfolio of real app and website case studies gets you interviews.
careers.outlook: Strong remote demand as businesses build apps and AI products that people need to understand and trust.

careers.title: Fashion / Textile Designer
careers.route: Fashion or textile design degree with portfolio-based admission, then internships with brands or boutiques; many designers go on to start their own label.
careers.outlook: Desi fashion is global: wedding wear, modest fashion and online boutiques sell from Lahore to London, and sustainability is the new edge.

careers.title: Screenwriter (TV, film and streaming)
careers.route: Any degree, often media, film or literature; writing samples, workshops, fellowships and pitching to production houses matter far more than formal qualifications.
careers.outlook: Desi dramas and films have huge global audiences, and streaming platforms now commission South Asian stories in many countries.

careers.title: Content Writer / Copywriter (remote)
careers.route: Any degree or none: strong writing in English (or another language you know well), a portfolio of samples, freelance platforms and agency internships.
careers.outlook: Steady, but AI means clients now pay for voice, strategy and editing skill rather than word count.

careers.title: Video Editor / Content Creator
careers.route: No degree required: short courses in Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve or CapCut, then a self-built portfolio of edits for creators and brands.
careers.outlook: High demand worldwide for short-form video editors; creators who build their own audience can turn it into a business.

careers.title: Animator / Game Artist
careers.route: Degree in animation, game art or multimedia, or online courses; studios hire on your portfolio and art tests rather than your grades.
careers.outlook: Mobile games, streaming animation and remote studio work keep growing; AI handles some grunt work, so strong fundamentals stand out.

careers.title: Wedding & Brand Photographer / Videographer
careers.route: No degree needed: short courses and a few seasons assisting an established studio while you build your own portfolio and client list.
careers.outlook: Desi wedding season, from Birmingham to Karachi to Houston, keeps skilled photographers booked, and brands always need fresh content.

careers.title: Interior Designer
careers.route: Interior design degree or diploma, plus software skills such as SketchUp; some countries license the title, and a portfolio is what wins clients.
careers.outlook: Growing with new housing and a strong renovation culture; virtual design and 3D renders add remote work.

careers.title: Journalist / Digital Media Producer
careers.route: Journalism, media or any degree, plus a portfolio of published work; newsroom internships, student media and your own newsletter or channel open doors.
careers.outlook: Traditional newsrooms are shrinking, while digital video, podcasts, newsletters and fact-checking roles grow.

careers.title: Calligrapher / Artisan Entrepreneur
careers.route: No degree needed: learn from an ustaad, in workshops or through online classes, then sell through Instagram, Etsy, craft fairs and commissions.
careers.outlook: A niche but meaningful path; calligraphy, henna and handmade crafts sell well to desi families worldwide, especially around weddings and festivals.

A.subjects: Art & Design, English Literature, Media Studies or Design & Technology at A-level, IB or high-school level; Maths and Physics alongside Art for architecture; Computer Science for digital design, animation and UI/UX.

S.name: Social
S.summary: Social people are energised by helping others learn, grow and feel understood. You are the friend people call at 2 am, the sibling who explains maths to younger cousins, the one who quietly checks that everyone at the dawat has been served. You notice how people feel, and you care about fairness and kindness. You value relationships, service and meaningful work, and you are happiest teaching, guiding, caring, counselling or supporting people, especially when you can see the difference you make.

careers.title: Teacher / Lecturer
careers.route: Degree in your subject plus a teaching qualification (PGCE, B.Ed or a state teaching licence), which differs by country; lecturing usually needs a master's or PhD.
careers.outlook: Steady demand everywhere, especially for maths, science and special-needs teachers; international schools hire across borders.

careers.title: Online Tutor (remote)
careers.route: No degree needed to start: subject, language or faith-teaching expertise, a certificate such as TEFL, and students found through tutoring platforms or word of mouth.
careers.outlook: Large, steady demand from families across time zones; AI handles drills, so human tutors win on motivation, patience and trust.

careers.title: Nurse
careers.route: Nursing degree (three to four years), or a diploma in some countries, then a national licensing exam; nurses moving abroad usually sit an extra exam.
careers.outlook: Short-staffed almost everywhere, with strong demand in the UK, US, Canada, Australia and the Gulf.

careers.title: Physiotherapist
careers.route: Physiotherapy degree (a BSc in the UK, a Doctor of Physical Therapy in the US and some other countries), then registration with your national health regulator.
careers.outlook: Growing in hospitals, sports clubs and home-visit services as populations age and stay active longer.

careers.title: Counsellor / School Psychologist
careers.route: Psychology or counselling degree, then a master's or accredited counselling diploma with supervised practice hours; regulation differs widely between countries.
careers.outlook: Schools, universities, workplaces and online platforms are hiring more counsellors, and stigma in desi families is slowly lifting.

careers.title: Nutritionist / Dietitian
careers.route: Accredited nutrition and dietetics degree plus supervised placements; 'dietitian' is a protected title in many countries, while 'nutritionist' often isn't.
careers.outlook: Growing interest in healthy eating, hospital roles and online consulting, with real demand for advice that respects desi food.

careers.title: HR Professional
careers.route: Business or psychology degree, or any degree plus HR certification (CIPD, SHRM or a local equivalent); graduate schemes are a common way in.
careers.outlook: Every growing company needs people skills; AI handles CV screening, so HR now focuses on culture, wellbeing and remote teams.

careers.title: Social Worker / Development Professional
careers.route: Social work degree with supervised placements and registration where required; development roles favour sociology or development studies plus NGO internships.
careers.outlook: Steady in local councils, NGOs and international agencies, especially in health, education, refugee and climate-recovery work.

careers.title: Speech or Occupational Therapist
careers.route: Degree or master's in speech and language therapy or occupational therapy, with clinical placements and registration with your country's regulator.
careers.outlook: A small field with unmet demand, particularly in children's services and multilingual families.

careers.title: Paramedic / Emergency Medical Technician
careers.route: EMT certificate courses take weeks to months in many countries; paramedic roles need a diploma or degree, plus fitness and driving tests.
careers.outlook: A respected public-service role with regular recruitment; ageing populations keep emergency services busy.

careers.title: Customer Success Specialist (remote)
careers.route: Any degree or none: strong English, clear writing and patience; start in customer support at a remote-first company and build experience and references.
careers.outlook: A large remote market; chatbots handle simple tickets, so people who solve tricky problems and keep clients happy are valued.

careers.title: Montessori / Early Childhood Educator
careers.route: Montessori or early-years diploma (often around one year) after school, with placements; some countries require a licence or degree for lead roles.
careers.outlook: Steady demand in nurseries and preschools, and a route to running your own home-based childcare.

S.subjects: Biology and Chemistry at A-level, IB or high-school level for nursing, physiotherapy, nutrition and therapy careers; Psychology, Sociology and English for counselling, teaching and social work; Business or Economics for HR.

E.name: Enterprising
E.summary: Enterprising people want to make things happen and bring others along. You enjoy persuading, leading, negotiating and taking calculated risks. You might be the one who started selling something at school, who bargains with every shopkeeper in the bazaar, or who ends up organising the cousins' trip because nobody else will decide. You value influence, achievement and results, and you are happiest when you can lead a team, build a business, close a deal or turn an idea into something that earns.

careers.title: Entrepreneur / Startup Founder
careers.route: Any degree or none, though business, computing or engineering helps; build a small product, join a university incubator or accelerator, then pitch investors.
careers.outlook: Funding is selective in 2026, but lean, profitable startups built with AI tools can reach customers worldwide on tiny budgets.

careers.title: E-commerce Seller
careers.route: No degree needed: free online courses, then start on Instagram, Etsy, Amazon, Shopify or a local marketplace and scale with ads and good reviews.
careers.outlook: A large, growing global market; desi fashion, food and gifts sell well to diaspora customers across borders.

careers.title: Sales / Business Development Executive
careers.route: Any degree, or none for some roles; graduate sales schemes and interviews where communication, resilience and hitting targets matter most.
careers.outlook: Every company needs revenue; remote B2B sales roles are growing, and AI handles the admin, not the relationship.

careers.title: Digital Marketing Specialist
careers.route: Marketing degree, or Google and Meta certificates plus a portfolio of real campaigns; agency internships and freelance clients build experience fast.
careers.outlook: Very high demand as businesses move online; AI makes content cheap, so strategy and data skills are where the value is.

careers.title: Lawyer
careers.route: Law degree (LLB), or a first degree then a JD in the US and Canada, followed by bar or solicitor exams; routes differ sharply by country.
careers.outlook: Competitive but steady; corporate, immigration, tech and AI law are growing niches, while AI takes over routine document work.

careers.title: Civil Servant (policy, foreign service and administration)
careers.route: Any degree, then your country's competitive civil service exam or graduate scheme; most posts require citizenship and some need security clearance.
careers.outlook: Highly competitive, respected and stable; serious preparation is essential, and policy roles increasingly value data skills.

careers.title: Banker / Relationship Manager
careers.route: Business, finance or economics degree, or an MBA later; bank graduate schemes and management trainee programmes with tests and interviews.
careers.outlook: Steady; digital banking is shifting roles towards technology, compliance and advisory work.

careers.title: Real Estate Consultant
careers.route: No degree needed: join an established agency and learn the trade; many places require a licence exam, such as a US state licence or Dubai's RERA certification.
careers.outlook: Cyclical but always active; honesty and transparency set the best agents apart, especially with overseas buyers.

careers.title: Event Planner (weddings and corporate)
careers.route: No degree required, though hospitality or events courses help; assist an established planner, then build your own vendor network and portfolio.
careers.outlook: Desi weddings from Toronto to Dubai to Lahore are a big year-round business, and corporate events fill the gaps between seasons.

careers.title: Product Manager (tech)
careers.route: Computing, business or engineering degree plus product courses; most people move in from associate product manager, analyst, design or engineering roles.
careers.outlook: A well-paid role in tech companies and remote startups; AI products need PMs who understand both users and the technology.

careers.title: Restaurant / Food Business Owner
careers.route: Culinary or hospitality diploma optional; start with a home kitchen, food stall or cloud kitchen, with the food-safety licence your local authority requires.
careers.outlook: Delivery apps and the global love of desi food keep the sector growing, though margins are thin and location matters.

careers.title: Import / Export Trader
careers.route: Business degree or hands-on experience; learn customs, shipping and trade finance, then register with customs and a chamber of commerce in your country.
careers.outlook: Openings in textiles, food, spices, sports goods and IT services, with diaspora networks linking South Asia, the Gulf and the West.

E.subjects: Business, Economics and Maths at A-level, IB or high-school level for business and finance; English, History, Politics or Law for law and the civil service; Computer Science for tech product roles.

C.name: Conventional
C.summary: Conventional people bring order to chaos. You like clear systems, accurate records and knowing exactly what is expected. You might be the one who tracks who owes what after a family trip, files every receipt, or notices when the electricity bill doesn't add up. You would rather do something right than do it fast and sloppy. You value accuracy, stability and responsibility, and you are happiest organising data, managing money, following procedures and building systems that other people can rely on without a second thought.

careers.title: Chartered Accountant (CA)
careers.route: Qualify through your country's chartered or certified accountancy body (ICAEW, CPA, ICAI, ICAP and others), with paid training at a firm; school-leaver routes exist in some countries.
careers.outlook: Consistently in demand; accountants lead finance, audit and tax worldwide, and as AI automates bookkeeping, advisory skills matter more.

careers.title: ACCA Professional
careers.route: ACCA qualification, often alongside or after a degree; you can register straight after A-levels or an equivalent and study while you work.
careers.outlook: Recognised worldwide and well suited to remote finance roles, the Gulf or moving abroad.

careers.title: Management Accountant (CIMA / CMA)
careers.route: CIMA, the US CMA or a national cost-accounting body, often alongside a degree; many people study part-time while working in a finance team.
careers.outlook: Steady demand in manufacturing, costing and corporate finance, with more focus on analytics and planning.

careers.title: Auditor / Tax Consultant
careers.route: Accounting, finance or business degree, then professional exams and training under senior consultants; tax rules are national, so expertise is country-specific.
careers.outlook: Steady as tax and reporting rules grow more complex; AI audits the routine, people handle the judgement calls.

careers.title: Bookkeeper (remote)
careers.route: No degree required: QuickBooks or Xero certification and a bookkeeping course, then freelance platforms and remote accounting firms.
careers.outlook: Strong remote demand from small businesses in the US, UK and Australia; AI handles data entry, so clients pay for accuracy and advice.

careers.title: Medical Billing & Coding Specialist (remote)
careers.route: No degree required: short certification courses such as CPC (US) or clinical coding training (UK), then billing companies or hospital admin teams.
careers.outlook: An established industry with many remote and outsourced roles; AI-assisted coding is shifting work towards auditing and complex cases.

careers.title: Banking Operations Officer
careers.route: Business, accounting or finance degree; bank graduate or operations programmes with aptitude tests and interviews, and compliance certifications help later.
careers.outlook: Steady; digital banking still needs careful operations, compliance and fraud-prevention staff.

careers.title: Government Officer (administration track)
careers.route: Any degree, or school qualifications for junior grades; competitive public service tests and interviews, which differ by country and usually require citizenship.
careers.outlook: Stable, respected roles; competition is high, but recruitment is regular.

careers.title: Supply Chain / Logistics Coordinator
careers.route: Supply chain, business or any degree; graduate schemes and logistics firms are the way in, with certifications such as CIPS or APICS later.
careers.outlook: Growing with e-commerce, ports and shifting global trade routes; AI forecasting still needs people who understand the real world.

careers.title: Executive Virtual Assistant (remote)
careers.route: No degree required: strong English, Excel, Google Workspace and calendar skills; start on freelance platforms or with virtual-assistant agencies.
careers.outlook: High demand from busy founders worldwide; AI handles simple tasks, so reliability and judgement are your selling point.

careers.title: Software QA Tester
careers.route: Computing degree, or ISTQB certification and test-automation courses; internships at software companies and a portfolio of test projects get you started.
careers.outlook: Steady demand, though manual testing is shrinking as AI tools spread, so automation and AI-testing skills matter most.

careers.title: Actuary / Statistician
careers.route: Degree in statistics, actuarial science or maths, then professional actuarial exams (IFoA, SOA or CAS) taken while working; national statistics offices hire too.
careers.outlook: A small, well-paid niche in insurance, pensions, climate risk and research.

C.subjects: Maths, Accounting, Economics and Business at A-level, IB or high-school level for accountancy, ACCA and banking; Maths, Statistics and Computer Science for data and QA roles; Further Maths for actuarial science.

pairs_note: Your Career Compass gives you a three-letter code, like SAE or IRC, made from your three strongest interest areas in order. The first letter is your strongest pull; the second and third shape how you like to use it. An IR person loves investigating hands-on problems, like an engineer or lab scientist, while an IS person enjoys investigating people, like a psychologist or doctor. Read the careers for all three letters and look for overlaps. Letters that sit next to each other on the Holland hexagon (R-I-A-S-E-C) blend naturally; opposite letters, like A and C, suggest unusually broad interests.
